title: Grade 5 Math — Mon, Jun 23
description: Volume and Capacity — Day 1 of 5: What is volume? Unit cubes and counting
subject: mathematics

questions.question: Volume is the amount of space a 3D object occupies. What unit is commonly used for volume?
questions.explanation: Volume is measured in cubic units — cm³ (cubic centimetres) for small objects, m³ (cubic metres) for large ones. 'Cubic' refers to 3 dimensions: length × breadth × height.

questions.question: A unit cube has all sides equal to 1 cm. Its volume is:
questions.explanation: Volume of a unit cube = 1 × 1 × 1 = 1 cm³. It occupies exactly 1 cubic centimetre of space.

questions.question: A shape is made of unit cubes arranged in a single layer: 3 cubes wide and 2 cubes long. How many unit cubes are there?
The same 3×2 base arrangement is stacked 4 layers high. Total unit cubes =
A solid shape is made by stacking unit cubes: first layer has 8 cubes, second layer has 8 cubes. Total volume =
questions.explanation: Each layer = 8 unit cubes. 2 layers = 8 × 2 = 16 unit cubes = 16 cm³.

questions.question: Why do we measure volume in CUBIC units (cm³) rather than square units (cm²)?
options: Volume requires 3 dimensions (length × breadth × height). Multiplying 3 lengths gives cubic units. Square units (cm²) only describe area (2 dimensions).
Square units cannot be used in maths
questions.explanation: Area = 2 dimensions → cm². Volume = 3 dimensions → cm³. When we multiply 3 measurements each in cm, we get cm × cm × cm = cm³.

The volume of 1 m³ in terms of cm³ is:
questions.explanation: 1 m = 100 cm. Volume conversion: 1 m³ = 100 × 100 × 100 = 1,000,000 cm³ (one million cubic centimetres).

questions.question: A shape has two parts: Part A = 12 unit cubes, Part B = 8 unit cubes. Total volume =
questions.explanation: Total = 12 + 8 = 20 unit cubes = 20 cm³. For composite (L-shaped, etc.) solids, break into parts and add volumes.

questions.question: A student counts cubes and gets 36 for a cuboid. If the cuboid is 4 cm long and 3 cm wide, how many layers high is it?
questions.explanation: Base = 4 × 3 = 12 cubes per layer. Layers = 36 ÷ 12 = 3 layers. Height = 3 cm.

questions.question: An L-shaped solid is made of unit cubes. The longer arm has 20 cubes, the shorter arm has 12 cubes, but 4 cubes overlap in the corner. Actual total =
questions.explanation: When shapes overlap, subtract the overlap. 20 + 12 − 4 = 28 unit cubes total.

questions.question: Two cuboids: Box P = 4×3×2 = 24 cm³. Box Q = 6×2×2 = 24 cm³. A student says 'they are the same.' Is this correct?
options: Yes — same volume means they are identical
Yes — same volume but DIFFERENT shapes. Two objects can have equal volumes but completely different dimensions.
questions.explanation: Volume = 24 cm³ for both. BUT shapes are different (P is shorter/wider, Q is longer/thinner). Equal volume does NOT mean identical shape. This is a key concept.

Ravi has a box that holds exactly 60 unit cubes. Priya has a box that holds 5 layers of 12 cubes each. Whose box is bigger?
options: They are the same size — both hold 60 unit cubes = 60 cm³
questions.explanation: Ravi = 60 cubes = 60 cm³. Priya = 5 × 12 = 60 cubes = 60 cm³. Both boxes have the same volume (60 cm³) even if their shapes may differ.
